reason: The artifact has no test.py/get_inputs, so problem.txt is the operative contract, and it requires exact binary16 round-to-nearest-even output bit patterns for every finite FP16 input, with reference() as the bit-exact oracle and "one failing legal input is evidence against the implementation." Claim c1 is confirmed, in_scope, with scope evidence citing this stated input domain. The t25 exhaustive probe swept all 63,488 finite FP16 encodings and found 7 legal inputs (e.g. x = 0.0029296875, -0.00927734375) whose kernel outputs differ from the reference oracle by exactly one adjacent FP16 code — wrong-side rounding at FP16 tie boundaries caused by the FP32-internal arithmetic (libdevice.exp + FP32 add + div_rn) landing on the wrong side of the halfway point. The independent FP64-sigmoid + numpy-RNE spot check agrees with reference() in all 7 cases, so the oracle is trustworthy and the kernel is the deviating side. Since the contract explicitly requires this exact rounding behavior, the deviation is a defect even though each mismatch is only one ulp; no tolerance clause accommodates it. c2 (subnormal-output precision) and c3 (signed zeros / underflow-to-zero) were rebutted on their specific hypotheses, so they do not affect the verdict. The Skeptic reviewed the final evidence and recorded no new claims.
